---
title: "Main Experiments"
author: "Przemek Marcowski"
---

This notebook holds the seven main experiments on how effort shapes hedonic
(liking) versus monetary (price) value: laboratory stepping (Experiment 1),
observed effort (Experiment 2), within-subjects clicking (Experiment 3),
effort-contingent perceptual reveal (Experiment 4, followed by its post-effort
target reveal, Experiment S7), cognitive effort (Experiment 5), and buying and
selling prices between and within subjects (Experiments 6A and 6B).
Every experiment follows one rhythm: one factorial omnibus model, the linear
effort slope of each judgment with its confidence interval, and the slope
difference, which is the dissociation test. Time-on-task checks, task-load
moderation, naive beliefs, and participant rating profiles follow where the
design recorded them. Prepared data are read from each experiment's `data/`
directory.

| Section | Reported as | Figures |
|---|---|---|
| Experiment 1: Laboratory Stepping | Experiment 1 | 2; S6, S7, S8 |
| Experiment 2: Observed Effort | Experiment 2 | 3 |
| Experiment 3: Within-Subjects Clicking | Experiment 3 | 4 |
| Experiment 4: Effort-Contingent Reveal | Experiment 4; Experiment S7 in the Supplemental Material | 5; S15 |
| Experiment 5: Cognitive Effort | Experiment 5; task-by-task detail in the Supplemental Material | 6; S12, S13 |
| Experiment 6A: Buying and Selling Prices, Between Subjects | Experiment 6A | 7 |
| Experiment 6B: Buying and Selling Prices, Within Subjects | Experiment 6B | 7 |

```{r setup, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(afex)
library(emmeans)
library(here)

here::i_am("analysis/main.qmd")
set.seed(42)
emm_options(lmer.df = "satterthwaite", lmerTest.limit = 2e+5)

source(here("R/functions.R"))
```

# Experiment 1: Laboratory Stepping

Participants performed a stepping task at three effort levels to collect
artworks, then rated them on one of three between-subjects scales: liking,
wanting, or price. The confirmatory test is the condition-by-effort
interaction—whether effort moves hedonic and monetary judgments in
different directions. Every participant who completed the session enters the
analyses.

```{r stepping-data}
stepping_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/stepping/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  mutate(
    subjID = as.factor(subjID),
    sex = as.factor(sex),
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Liking", "Value", "Wanting")),
    across(c(rel_liking, rel_value, rel_wanting), ~factor(.x, levels = c("Less", "Neither", "More"))),
    across(-where(is.factor), \(x) as.numeric(x))
  )

n_stepping <- n_distinct(stepping_data$subjID)
```

The sample comprises `r n_stepping` participants.

```{r stepping-sample}
stepping_data %>%
  group_by(subjID) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  summarize(
    n = n_distinct(subjID),
    mean_age = mean(age), sd_age = sd(age),
    n_male = n_distinct(subjID[sex == "Male"]),
    n_female = n_distinct(subjID[sex == "Female"]),
    n_other = n_distinct(subjID[sex == "Other"])
  )
```

## Main Analysis

We fit one factorial model with rating condition and effort level as fixed
effects and a random intercept per participant, and the interaction carries
the dissociation.

```{r stepping-omnibus}
stepping_omnibus <- mixed(
  rating ~ condition * effort_level + (1 | subjID),
  data = stepping_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(stepping_omnibus)
```

A second model with effort as a numeric level index gives the linear effort
slope of each scale, and the pairwise slope differences test whether the
scales diverge.

```{r stepping-slopes}
stepping_trend <- mixed(
  rating ~ condition * effort_num + (1 | subjID),
  data = stepping_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control, progress = FALSE
)

stepping_slopes <- emtrends(stepping_trend, ~condition, var = "effort_num", infer = TRUE)
stepping_slopes

stepping_slope_diffs <- withr::with_seed(
  42, pairs(stepping_slopes, infer = TRUE, adjust = "mvt", reverse = TRUE)
)
stepping_slope_diffs
```

::: {.callout-note title="Key result"}
```{r stepping-key-result}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
report_slopes(stepping_slopes, stepping_slope_diffs, labels = c(Value = "Price"))
```
:::

```{r stepping-plot}
stepping_means <- as.data.frame(emmeans(stepping_omnibus, ~ effort_level * condition))

stepping_plot <-
  stepping_means %>%
  mutate(
    condition = recode(condition, "Value" = "Price"),
    condition = fct_relevel(condition, "Liking", "Wanting")
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = effort_level, y = emmean, group = condition, colour = condition)) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL),
    width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_evl() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~., labels = label_price)
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~condition) +
  labs(title = "Liking, Wanting, and Price", x = "Effort Level", y = "Mean Rating") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 5)) +
  theme_evl()

save_figure(stepping_plot, "stepping_ratings")
```

## Time on Task

The effort manipulation also lengthens trials, so the interaction should hold
with performance time in the model.

```{r stepping-omnibus-time}
stepping_omnibus_time <- mixed(
  rating ~ condition * effort_level + effort_time + (1 | subjID),
  data = stepping_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(stepping_omnibus_time)
```

Time on task should track effort level but not the judgment participants were
assigned to make.

```{r stepping-duration}
stepping_duration <- mixed(
  effort_time ~ condition * effort_level + (1 | subjID),
  data = stepping_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(stepping_duration)
```

## Moderation by Task Load

Performed steps and the post-task NASA-TLX score, both rescaled to the unit
interval, enter a three-way model with rating condition. The exploratory
question is whether effort moves ratings more among participants who found the
task more demanding.

```{r stepping-task-load}
stepping_task_load_data <- stepping_data %>%
  select(everything(), effort = effort_trials, moder = adjusted_overall) %>%
  mutate(across(c(effort, moder), ~scales::rescale(.x, c(0, 1))))

stepping_task_load <- lmer(rating ~ effort * moder * condition + (1 | subjID),
                           data = stepping_task_load_data)

anova(stepping_task_load, type = 3)
```

```{r stepping-task-load-plot}
stepping_task_load_plot <- interactions::interact_plot(
  stepping_task_load,
  pred = "effort",
  modx = "moder", mod2 = "condition",
  legend.main = "Task Load (NASA-TLX)",
  line.thickness = 0.7,
  modx.labels = c("-1 SD", "Mean", "+1 SD"),
  mod2.values = c("Liking", "Wanting", "Value"),
  mod2.labels = c("Liking", "Wanting", "Price"),
  main.title = "Moderation of Ratings by Task Load"
) +
  # interact_plot interpolates its own gradient for a numeric moderator, so the
  # palette steps are mapped onto the moderator groups here
  aes(colour = modx_group) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "-1 SD" = evl_colours[["Teal Light"]], "Mean" = evl_colours[["Teal"]],
      "+1 SD" = evl_colours[["Teal Dark"]]
    ),
    name = "Task Load (NASA-TLX)"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1), labels = c("0", "0.5", "1")) +
  labs(x = "Performed Steps (Proportion of Maximum)", y = "Mean Rating") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 5)) +
  theme_evl(legend = "bottom")

save_figure(stepping_task_load_plot, "stepping_task_load_moderation")
```

## Beliefs

Participants also stated how they believed effort relates to liking, price,
and wanting, and the proportions summarize those naive theories.

```{r stepping-beliefs}
stepping_beliefs <-
  stepping_data %>%
  select(subjID, contains("rel_")) %>%
  group_by(subjID) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename("Liking" = "rel_liking", "Price" = "rel_value", "Wanting" = "rel_wanting") %>%
  pivot_longer(-subjID, names_to = "belief", values_to = "type") %>%
  janitor::tabyl(belief, type) %>%
  janitor::adorn_totals("col") %>%
  mutate(across(c(2, 3, 4), ~ round((.x / Total), 3)))

stepping_beliefs
```

```{r stepping-beliefs-plot}
stepping_beliefs_plot <-
  stepping_beliefs %>%
  pivot_longer(c(-belief, -Total), names_to = "type", values_to = "prop") %>%
  mutate(
    belief = factor(belief, levels = c("Liking", "Wanting", "Price")),
    type = factor(type, levels = c("Less", "Neither", "More"))
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = type, y = prop)) +
  geom_col(colour = "black") +
  labs(title = "Beliefs About Effort", x = "Belief", y = "Proportion") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~belief) +
  theme_evl()

save_figure(stepping_beliefs_plot, "stepping_beliefs")
```

Within the liking condition, ratings should not depend on the stated
effort–liking belief if the effect is not a naive-theory artifact.

```{r stepping-beliefs-model}
stepping_beliefs_model <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_level * rel_liking + (1 | subjID),
  data = stepping_data[stepping_data$condition == "Liking", ],
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(stepping_beliefs_model)
```

```{r stepping-beliefs-ratings-plot}
effort_level_colours <- c(Low = "#704B00", Medium = "#A06D00", High = evl_colours[["Liking"]])
effort_level_shapes <- c(Low = 16, Medium = 15, High = 17)

stepping_beliefs_ratings_plot <- stepping_data %>%
  filter(condition %in% "Liking") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = rel_liking, y = rating, group = effort_level, colour = effort_level)) +
  stat_summary(
    geom = "errorbar", fun.data = "mean_cl_normal",
    width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    aes(shape = effort_level),
    geom = "point", fun = "mean", position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = effort_level_colours, name = "Effort Level") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = effort_level_shapes, name = "Effort Level") +
  labs(
    title = "Effort-Liking Beliefs and Ratings of Liking",
    x = "Liking Belief", y = "Mean Rating"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 5)) +
  theme_evl(legend = "bottom")

save_figure(stepping_beliefs_ratings_plot, "stepping_beliefs_liking")
```

## Rating Profiles

Each participant's mean rating at high versus low effort classifies them as
increasing or decreasing on their scale, and the proportions describe how
general the effect is across people.

```{r stepping-profiles}
stepping_profiles <- derive_effort_profiles(stepping_data, id = "subjID")

summarize_effort_profiles(stepping_profiles)
```

# Experiment 2: Observed Effort

Participants watched another person perform the stepping effort at three
levels and rated the collected artworks on a liking or a price scale (between
subjects). If the dissociation requires performing the effort, the slopes
should flatten here. If effort information suffices, they should mirror
Experiment 1. Every participant who completed the session enters the analyses.

```{r observed-data}
observed_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/observed/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  mutate(
    id = as.factor(id),
    scale_type = factor(scale_type, levels = c("Liking", "Value"))
  )

n_observed <- n_distinct(observed_data$id)
```

The sample comprises `r n_observed` participants.

```{r observed-sample}
observed_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  summarize(
    n = n_distinct(id),
    mean_age = mean(age), sd_age = sd(age),
    n_male = n_distinct(id[gender == "Male"]),
    n_female = n_distinct(id[gender == "Female"]),
    n_other = n_distinct(id[gender == "Other"])
  )
```

## Main Analysis

One factorial model with rating scale and effort level as fixed effects and a
random intercept per observer carries the dissociation in its interaction.

```{r observed-omnibus}
observed_omnibus <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_level * scale_type + (1 | id),
  data = observed_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(observed_omnibus)
```

The effort slope of each scale, and their difference, come from the
numeric-effort model.

```{r observed-slopes}
observed_trend <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_num * scale_type + (1 | id),
  data = observed_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control, progress = FALSE
)

observed_slopes <- emtrends(observed_trend, ~scale_type, var = "effort_num", infer = TRUE)
observed_slopes

observed_slope_diffs <- pairs(observed_slopes, infer = TRUE, reverse = TRUE)
observed_slope_diffs
```

::: {.callout-note title="Key result"}
```{r observed-key-result}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
report_slopes(observed_slopes, observed_slope_diffs, labels = c(Value = "Price"))
```
:::

```{r observed-plot}
observed_means <- as.data.frame(emmeans(observed_omnibus, ~ effort_level * scale_type))

observed_plot <-
  observed_means %>%
  mutate(scale_type = recode(scale_type, "Value" = "Price")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = effort_level, y = emmean, group = scale_type, colour = scale_type)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_evl() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~., labels = label_price)
  ) +

    x = "Effort Level", y = "Mean Rating"

  facet_wrap(~scale_type) +
  theme_evl()

save_figure(observed_plot, "observed_ratings")
```

## Rating Profiles

Each participant's mean rating at high versus low effort classifies them as
increasing or decreasing on their scale.

```{r observed-profiles}
observed_profiles <- derive_effort_profiles(observed_data, groups = "scale_type")

summarize_effort_profiles(observed_profiles, groups = "scale_type")
```

# Experiment 3: Within-Subjects Clicking

Participants collected artworks with a clicking task at three effort levels
and rated them on liking in one block and on price in the other, so each
person supplies both judgments. The design, sample size, and exclusions were
preregistered: the analyzed sample excludes participants who failed the
attention check, whose summed clicking time exceeded the sample mean by more
than 2.5 SD, or who did not complete the post-survey, and a skipped rating
drops only its trial. The dissociation prediction is a negative liking slope
and a positive price slope across effort.

```{r clicking-within-data}
clicking_within_post <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/clicking_within/data/post.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(id = as.factor(id))

clicking_within_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/clicking_within/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  mutate(
    id = as.factor(id),
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Liking", "Value"))
  )

n_clicking_within <- n_distinct(clicking_within_data$id)
```

The analyzed sample comprises `r n_clicking_within` participants.

```{r clicking-within-sample}
clicking_within_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  summarize(
    n = n_distinct(id),
    mean_age = mean(age), sd_age = sd(age),
    n_male = n_distinct(id[gender == "Male"]),
    n_female = n_distinct(id[gender == "Female"]),
    n_other = n_distinct(id[gender == "Other"])
  )
```

## Main Analysis

One factorial model with judgment and effort level as within-subjects fixed
effects and a random intercept per participant carries the dissociation in its
interaction.

```{r clicking-within-omnibus}
clicking_within_omnibus <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_level * condition + (1 | id),
  data = clicking_within_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(clicking_within_omnibus)
```

The effort slope of each judgment, and their difference, come from the
numeric-effort model.

```{r clicking-within-slopes}
clicking_within_trend <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_num * condition + (1 | id),
  data = clicking_within_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control, progress = FALSE
)

clicking_within_slopes <- emtrends(
  clicking_within_trend, ~condition, var = "effort_num", infer = TRUE
)
clicking_within_slopes

clicking_within_slope_diffs <- pairs(clicking_within_slopes, infer = TRUE, reverse = TRUE)
clicking_within_slope_diffs
```

::: {.callout-note title="Key result"}
```{r clicking-within-key-result}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
report_slopes(clicking_within_slopes, clicking_within_slope_diffs, labels = c(Value = "Price"))
```
:::

```{r clicking-within-plot}
clicking_within_means <- as.data.frame(
  emmeans(clicking_within_omnibus, ~ effort_level * condition)
)

clicking_within_plot <-
  clicking_within_means %>%
  mutate(condition = recode(condition, "Value" = "Price")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = effort_level, y = emmean, group = condition, colour = condition)) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL),
    width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_evl() +
  # The means and their intervals lie between 2 and 4, so the axis shows that window
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2, 4, 0.5), sec.axis = sec_axis(~., labels = label_price)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Ratings of Liking and Price",
    subtitle = "Within Subjects",
    x = "Effort Level", y = "Mean Rating"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(2, 4)) +
  facet_wrap(~condition) +
  theme_evl()

save_figure(clicking_within_plot, "clicking_within_ratings")
```

## Time on Task

The interaction should hold with clicking time in the model.

```{r clicking-within-omnibus-time}
clicking_within_omnibus_time <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_level * condition + effort_time + (1 | id),
  data = clicking_within_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(clicking_within_omnibus_time)
```

Time on task should track effort level but not the judgment made on the trial,
which varies within participants here.

```{r clicking-within-duration}
clicking_within_duration <- mixed(
  effort_time ~ condition * effort_level + (1 | id),
  data = clicking_within_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(clicking_within_duration)
```

## Beliefs

Everyone rated on both scales, so the post-survey beliefs about how effort
relates to liking and to value are summarized for the whole sample.

```{r clicking-within-beliefs}
clicking_within_beliefs <- belief_summary(clicking_within_post, group = NULL)

clicking_within_beliefs
```

## Rating Profiles

Each participant contributes a liking profile and a price profile, each the
direction of their mean rating from low to high effort.

```{r clicking-within-profiles}
clicking_within_profiles <- derive_effort_profiles(clicking_within_data)

summarize_effort_profiles(clicking_within_profiles)
```

Crossing each participant's liking profile with their price profile shows how
many people carry the dissociation individually, as decreasing liking together
with increasing price.

```{r clicking-within-profiles-crossed}
clicking_within_profile_counts <- crossed_profile_counts(clicking_within_profiles)

clicking_within_profile_counts

n_clicking_within_crossed <- sum(clicking_within_profile_counts$count)
```

The crossed counts cover the `r n_clicking_within_crossed` participants whose
ratings moved on both scales.

```{r clicking-within-profiles-crossed-plot}
show_figure(
  plot_crossed_profiles(clicking_within_profile_counts) +
    labs(title = "Profiles for Liking vs. Price")
)
```

# Experiment 4: Effort-Contingent Reveal

Participants advanced a walker toward a goal by pressing a key and collected
scrambled everyday objects whose presentation depended on the presses accepted
during the walk. A press counts as accepted only if it follows the previous
accepted press by at least the debounce interval, the shortest spacing at which
two presses both count, so faster presses are counted but do not move the
walker. Effort varied within participants at 30, 100, or 270 accepted presses,
and participants rated every object on either liking or price (between
subjects). These doses match the step counts of the laboratory stepping task
rather than the press counts of the clicking studies, so press totals and
durations here are not pooled with those studies. One collection used
progressive reveal, in which the object resolved as accepted presses
accumulated; a later collection, Experiment S7, revealed the object only once
the required presses were complete (post-effort target reveal). Participants
were not randomized between the two schedules, so each schedule is analyzed on
its own and no schedule contrast is estimated. Within each schedule, the
analyzed sample follows the preregistered exclusions, applied in data
preparation: no matching completed post-survey, chance-level recognition
memory (d′ ≤ 0), or summed walk time above the schedule mean by more than
2.5 SD. Repeat completion and viewport width are recorded as diagnostics and
do not alter inclusion. Because rating condition is between
subjects, condition differences at single effort levels confound with scale
anchoring, and the dissociation test is the difference between the price and
liking effort slopes.

```{r reveal-data}
reveal_all_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/reveal/data/main.csv"),
           col_types = cols(id = col_character(), .default = col_guess())) %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  mutate(
    id = as.factor(id),
    img = as.factor(img),
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Liking", "Value"))
  )

# Every completed session, the frame the exclusion flow starts from
reveal_all_complete <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/reveal/data/main_complete.csv"),
           col_types = cols(id = col_character(), .default = col_guess())) %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  mutate(
    id = as.factor(id),
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Liking", "Value"))
  )

reveal_all_memory <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/reveal/data/memory.csv"),
           col_types = cols(id = col_character(), .default = col_guess())) %>%
  mutate(
    id = as.factor(id),
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Liking", "Value"))
  )

reveal_data <- filter(reveal_all_data, reveal_assignment == "progressive")
reveal_complete <- filter(reveal_all_complete, reveal_assignment == "progressive")
reveal_memory <- filter(reveal_all_memory, reveal_assignment == "progressive")

reveal_endpoint_data <- filter(reveal_all_data, reveal_assignment == "endpoint")
reveal_endpoint_complete <- filter(reveal_all_complete, reveal_assignment == "endpoint")
reveal_endpoint_memory <- filter(reveal_all_memory, reveal_assignment == "endpoint")

n_reveal <- n_distinct(reveal_data$id)
n_reveal_complete <- n_distinct(reveal_complete$id)
n_reveal_endpoint <- n_distinct(reveal_endpoint_data$id)
n_reveal_endpoint_complete <- n_distinct(reveal_endpoint_complete$id)
```

## Progressive Reveal

Of `r n_reveal_complete` participants who completed the task, `r n_reveal`
remain after the preregistered exclusions and form the analytic sample.

```{r reveal-sample}
reveal_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  summarize(
    n = n_distinct(id),
    mean_age = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_age = sd(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_male = n_distinct(id[gender == "Male"]),
    n_female = n_distinct(id[gender == "Female"]),
    n_other = n_distinct(id[!gender %in% c("Male", "Female")]),
    n_liking = n_distinct(id[condition == "Liking"]),
    n_value = n_distinct(id[condition == "Value"])
  )
```

The exclusion flow, with the d′ and walk-time exclusions counted among the
participants with a completed post-survey (one participant can meet both), and
the diagnostics that are recorded but not applied:

```{r reveal-exclusions}
reveal_complete %>%
  distinct(id, has_post_survey, memory_pass, time_outlier_linked,
           primary_included, repeat_complete, viewport_width) %>%
  summarize(
    n_complete_sessions = n(),
    n_no_post_survey = sum(!has_post_survey),
    n_dprime_at_or_below_zero = sum(!memory_pass[has_post_survey]),
    n_time_outliers = sum(time_outlier_linked[has_post_survey]),
    n_analyzed = sum(primary_included),
    n_viewport_below_940 = sum(viewport_width[primary_included] < 940),
    n_repeat_completers = sum(repeat_complete[primary_included])
  )
```

### Memory Check

A recognition test on the collected objects shows whether participants
attended to what they collected, summarized by the sensitivity index d′.

```{r reveal-memory}
memory_summary(reveal_memory)
```

### Effort Manipulation Check

The walk is self-paced, so realized duration reflects both the assigned dose
and the participant's press rate, and the rejected-press proportion shows how
often the debounce interval bound.

```{r reveal-manipulation}
reveal_duration <- mixed(
  effort_trial_duration ~ effort_level + (1 | id),
  data = reveal_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)
nice(reveal_duration)

emmeans(reveal_duration, ~effort_level, infer = TRUE)

# Press mechanics and off-task focus loss across effort levels
reveal_data %>%
  mutate(accepted_press_rate = steps_required / effort_trial_duration) %>%
  group_by(effort_level) %>%
  summarize(
    accepted_presses = first(steps_required),
    duration_median_s = median(effort_trial_duration),
    accepted_rate_median_per_s = median(accepted_press_rate),
    rejected_press_proportion =
      sum(presses_rejected) / sum(steps_required + presses_rejected),
    focus_loss_trial_proportion = mean(walk_focus_lost > 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

### Main Analysis

One factorial model with effort level and rating condition as fixed effects and
a random intercept per participant carries the dissociation in its interaction.

```{r reveal-omnibus}
reveal_omnibus <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_level * condition + (1 | id),
  data = reveal_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(reveal_omnibus)
```

The effort slope of each judgment, and their difference, come from the
numeric-effort model.

```{r reveal-slopes}
reveal_trend <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_num * condition + (1 | id),
  data = reveal_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control, progress = FALSE
)

reveal_slopes <- emtrends(reveal_trend, ~condition, var = "effort_num", infer = TRUE)
reveal_slopes

reveal_slope_diffs <- pairs(reveal_slopes, infer = TRUE, reverse = TRUE)
reveal_slope_diffs
```

::: {.callout-note title="Key result"}
```{r reveal-key-result}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
report_slopes(reveal_slopes, reveal_slope_diffs, labels = c(Value = "Price"))
```
:::

```{r reveal-plot}
reveal_means <- as.data.frame(emmeans(reveal_omnibus, ~ effort_level * condition))

reveal_plot <-
  reveal_means %>%
  mutate(condition = recode(condition, "Value" = "Price")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = effort_level, y = emmean, group = condition, colour = condition)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_evl() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~., labels = label_price)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Ratings of Liking and Price",
    subtitle = "Progressive Reveal",
    x = "Effort Level", y = "Mean Rating"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 5)) +
  facet_wrap(~condition) +
  theme_evl()

save_figure(reveal_plot, "reveal_ratings")
```

### Time on Task

The interaction should hold with walk duration in the model.

```{r reveal-omnibus-time}
reveal_omnibus_time <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_level * condition + effort_trial_duration + (1 | id),
  data = reveal_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(reveal_omnibus_time)
```

Time on task should track effort level but not the judgment participants were
assigned to make.

```{r reveal-duration-by-condition}
reveal_duration_by_condition <- mixed(
  effort_trial_duration ~ effort_level * condition + (1 | id),
  data = reveal_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(reveal_duration_by_condition)
```

### Robustness: Maximal Random-Effects Structure

Effort varies within participants and objects are crossed with participants, so
the dissociation is refit with by-participant effort slopes and a crossed object
intercept, as a sensitivity check on the random-intercept model above.

```{r reveal-maximal}
reveal_trend_maximal <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_num * condition + (effort_num | id) + (1 | img),
  data = reveal_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control, progress = FALSE
)

nice(reveal_trend_maximal)
pairs(emtrends(reveal_trend_maximal, ~condition, var = "effort_num"), infer = TRUE, reverse = TRUE)
```

### Beliefs

Post-survey beliefs about how effort relates to liking and to value, pooled
over rating condition.

```{r reveal-beliefs}
belief_summary(reveal_data, group = NULL)
```

### Presentation Appraisals

Post-survey items asked whether the presses were experienced as instrumental,
necessary, and purposeful, on ordinal 1–5 scales.

```{r reveal-appraisals}
reveal_appraisals <-
  reveal_data %>%
  distinct(id, instrumental_task, necessary_effort, actions_purpose) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    c(instrumental_task, necessary_effort, actions_purpose),
    names_to = "appraisal",
    values_to = "response"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    appraisal = factor(
      appraisal,
      levels = c("instrumental_task", "necessary_effort", "actions_purpose"),
      labels = c("Effort Led to Objects", "Effort Was Necessary",
                 "Actions Served a Purpose")
    )
  )

reveal_appraisals %>%
  group_by(appraisal) %>%
  summarize(n = n(), mean = mean(response), sd = sd(response), .groups = "drop")

reveal_appraisals_plot <- reveal_appraisals %>%
  count(appraisal, response) %>%
  group_by(appraisal) %>%
  mutate(proportion = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(response, levels = 1:5), y = proportion)) +
  geom_col(colour = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~appraisal, nrow = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Post-Task Presentation Appraisals",
    x = "Response (1 = Low, 5 = High)", y = "Proportion"
  ) +
  theme_evl()

show_figure(reveal_appraisals_plot)
```

### Rating Profiles

Each participant's mean rating at high versus low effort classifies them as
increasing or decreasing.

```{r reveal-profiles}

summarize_effort_profiles(reveal_profiles)
```

```{r reveal-endpoint-sample}
  )
```

# Experiment 5: Cognitive Effort

One experiment with two between-subjects task arms replaces physical with
cognitive effort: letter transposition (Cogletters; shift each letter forward
in the alphabet by 1, 3, or 7 positions) and serial subtraction (Subtract-N;
count down by 1, 3, or 7). Rating condition (liking versus price) is between
subjects within each arm, and participants were randomly assigned to arm and
condition. The analyzed sample excludes participants without a completed
post-survey, with chance-level recognition memory (d′ ≤ 0), or whose summed
effort time exceeded the task mean by more than 2.5 SD, the preregistered
total-time rule. The effort levels index ordered task difficulty, so slopes
read as change per difficulty step.

```{r cognitive-data}
cogletters_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/cognitive/data/cogletters.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  mutate(
    id = as.factor(id),
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Liking", "Value"))
  )

subtractn_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/cognitive/data/subtractn.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  mutate(
    id = as.factor(id),
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Liking", "Value"))
  )

cognitive_memory <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/cognitive/data/memory.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    id = as.factor(id),
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Liking", "Value"))
  )

n_cogletters <- n_distinct(cogletters_data$id)
n_subtractn <- n_distinct(subtractn_data$id)
```

## Letter Transposition

The letter-transposition arm comprises `r n_cogletters` participants.

```{r cogletters-sample}
cogletters_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  summarize(
    n = n_distinct(id),
    mean_age = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_age = sd(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_male = n_distinct(id[gender == "Male"]),
    n_female = n_distinct(id[gender == "Female"]),
    n_other = n_distinct(id[!gender %in% c("Male", "Female")]),
    n_liking = n_distinct(id[condition == "Liking"]),
    n_value = n_distinct(id[condition == "Value"])
  )
```

### Memory Check

The recognition test on the collected objects, summarized by the sensitivity
index d′.

```{r cogletters-memory}
memory_summary(filter(cognitive_memory, id %in% unique(cogletters_data$id)))
```

### Effort Manipulation Check

The cipher offset should produce a difficulty gradient in transcription errors
and in time on task.

```{r cogletters-manipulation}
cogletters_errors <- mixed(
  effort_mismatches ~ effort_level + (1 | id),
  data = cogletters_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)
nice(cogletters_errors)
emmeans(cogletters_errors, ~effort_level, infer = TRUE)

cogletters_duration <- mixed(
  effort_trial_duration ~ effort_level + (1 | id),
  data = cogletters_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)
nice(cogletters_duration)
```

### Main Analysis

One factorial model with effort level and rating condition as fixed effects and
a random intercept per participant carries the dissociation in its interaction,
and the numeric-effort model gives the slope of each judgment and their
difference.

```{r cogletters-omnibus}
cogletters_omnibus <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_level * condition + (1 | id),
  data = cogletters_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(cogletters_omnibus)
```

```{r cogletters-slopes}
cogletters_trend <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_num * condition + (1 | id),
  data = cogletters_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control, progress = FALSE
)

cogletters_slopes <- emtrends(cogletters_trend, ~condition, var = "effort_num", infer = TRUE)
cogletters_slopes

cogletters_slope_diffs <- pairs(cogletters_slopes, infer = TRUE, reverse = TRUE)
cogletters_slope_diffs
```

```{r cogletters-key-result}
report_slopes(cogletters_slopes, cogletters_slope_diffs, labels = c(Value = "Price"))
```

### Moderation by Task Load

The post-task NASA-TLX score enters as a continuous moderator of the
dissociation.

```{r cogletters-task-load}

  rating ~ effort_num * condition * scale(nasa_tlx) + (1 | id),
  data = cogletters_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(cogletters_task_load)
```

### Moderation by Task Load

The post-task NASA-TLX score enters as a continuous moderator, and the effort
slopes at lower and higher task load (the mean minus and plus one SD) show
where the dissociation appears.

```{r subtractn-task-load}
subtractn_task_load <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_num * condition * scale(nasa_tlx) + (1 | id),
  data = subtractn_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(subtractn_task_load)

subtractn_task_load_mean <- mean(subtractn_data$nasa_tlx)
subtractn_task_load_sd <- sd(subtractn_data$nasa_tlx)
subtractn_task_load_levels <- subtractn_task_load_mean + c(-1, 1) * subtractn_task_load_sd

emtrends(
  subtractn_task_load,
  pairwise ~ condition | nasa_tlx,
  var = "effort_num",
  at = list(nasa_tlx = subtractn_task_load_levels),
  infer = TRUE
)

# the slopes at higher task load (+1 SD), carried into the summary
subtractn_high_load_slopes <- emtrends(
  subtractn_task_load, ~condition, var = "effort_num",
  at = list(nasa_tlx = subtractn_task_load_levels[2]), infer = TRUE
)
subtractn_high_load_slope_diffs <- pairs(subtractn_high_load_slopes, infer = TRUE, reverse = TRUE)
```

```{r subtractn-task-load-plot}
subtractn_task_load_means <- emmeans(
  subtractn_task_load,
  ~ effort_num | condition * nasa_tlx,
  at = list(effort_num = 1:3, nasa_tlx = subtractn_task_load_levels),
  infer = TRUE
)

subtractn_task_load_plot <-
  as.data.frame(subtractn_task_load_means) %>%
  mutate(
    condition = recode(condition, "Value" = "Price"),
    effort_level = factor(effort_num, levels = 1:3, labels = effort_levels),
    tlx_level = factor(
      nasa_tlx, levels = subtractn_task_load_levels,
      labels = c("Lower Task Load (-1 SD)", "Higher Task Load (+1 SD)")
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = effort_level, y = emmean, group = condition, colour = condition)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_evl() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~., labels = label_price)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Ratings of Liking and Price by Task Load",
    subtitle = "Serial Subtraction",
    x = "Effort Level", y = "Mean Rating"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 5)) +
  ggh4x::facet_nested_wrap(vars(tlx_level, condition), nrow = 2, axes = "x") +
  theme_evl()

save_figure(subtractn_task_load_plot, "cognitive_subtractn_task_load")
```

## Both Tasks

Both arms belong to a single experiment with random between-subjects
assignment to effort task, and the participant samples do not overlap, so the
arms pool with task as a between-subjects factor. Raw error counts differ by
task mechanics, so the proportion of erroneous responses per trial is the
commensurable error measure.

```{r cognitive-combined-data}
cognitive_data <-
  bind_rows(
    cogletters_data %>%
      mutate(effort_error_prop = effort_mismatches / (effort_matches + effort_mismatches)),
    subtractn_data %>%
      mutate(effort_error_prop = effort_incorrect_attempts / effort_total_attempts)
  ) %>%
  select(
    id, trial, condition, effort_task, effort_level, effort_num,
    rating, effort_error_prop, effort_trial_duration, nasa_tlx
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    id = factor(id),
    effort_task = factor(
      effort_task,
      levels = c("cogletters", "subtractn"),
      labels = c("Cogletters", "Subtract-N")
    )
  )
```

```{r cognitive-combined-n}
cognitive_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  count(effort_task, condition) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = n)
```

### Main Analysis

The pooled model averages over the task arms, and the task-adjusted test
follows.

```{r cognitive-omnibus}
cognitive_omnibus <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_level * condition + (1 | id),
  data = cognitive_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(cognitive_omnibus)
```

```{r cognitive-slopes}
cognitive_trend <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_num * condition + (1 | id),
  data = cognitive_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control, progress = FALSE
)

cognitive_slopes <- emtrends(cognitive_trend, ~condition, var = "effort_num", infer = TRUE)
cognitive_slopes

cognitive_slope_diffs <- pairs(cognitive_slopes, infer = TRUE, reverse = TRUE)
cognitive_slope_diffs
```

::: {.callout-note title="Key result"}
```{r cognitive-key-result}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
report_slopes(cognitive_slopes, cognitive_slope_diffs, labels = c(Value = "Price"))
```
:::

The experiment's figure shows the pooled model's means, averaged over the two
task arms; the task-by-task panels follow below.

```{r cognitive-pooled-plot}
cognitive_means <- as.data.frame(emmeans(cognitive_omnibus, ~ effort_level * condition))

cognitive_pooled_plot <-
  cognitive_means %>%
  mutate(condition = recode(condition, "Value" = "Price")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = effort_level, y = emmean, group = condition, colour = condition)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_evl() +
  # The means and their intervals lie between 2 and 4, so the axis shows that window
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2, 4, 0.5), sec.axis = sec_axis(~., labels = label_price)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Ratings of Liking and Price",
    subtitle = "Cognitive Effort, Both Tasks",
    x = "Effort Level", y = "Mean Rating"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(2, 4)) +
  facet_wrap(~condition) +
  theme_evl()

save_figure(cognitive_pooled_plot, "cognitive_pooled_ratings")
```

Task type enters as a third factor to test whether the dissociation differs
between the two arms.

```{r cognitive-task-omnibus}
cognitive_task_omnibus <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_level * condition * effort_task + (1 | id),
  data = cognitive_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(cognitive_task_omnibus)
```

```{r cognitive-by-task-plot}
cognitive_task_means <- as.data.frame(
  emmeans(cognitive_task_omnibus, ~ effort_level * condition * effort_task)
)

cognitive_by_task_plot <-
  cognitive_task_means %>%
  mutate(
    condition = recode(condition, "Value" = "Price"),
    effort_task = recode(effort_task, "Cogletters" = "Letter Transposition",
                         "Subtract-N" = "Serial Subtraction")
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = effort_level, y = emmean, group = condition, colour = condition)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_evl() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~., labels = label_price)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Ratings of Liking and Price",
    subtitle = "Cognitive Effort by Task",
    x = "Effort Level", y = "Mean Rating"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 5)) +
  ggh4x::facet_nested_wrap(vars(effort_task, condition), nrow = 2, axes = "x") +
  theme_evl()

save_figure(cognitive_by_task_plot, "cognitive_ratings_by_task")
```

The dissociation takes a different route in each task: in letter transposition
it holds across participants, and in serial subtraction only among
participants who found the task demanding (Serial Subtraction, Moderation by
Task Load).

### Time on Task

The task-adjusted interaction should hold with time on task in the model.

```{r cognitive-omnibus-time}
cognitive_omnibus_time <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_level * condition * effort_task + effort_trial_duration + (1 | id),
  data = cognitive_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(cognitive_omnibus_time)
```

Time on task should track effort level and task, but not the judgment
participants were assigned to make.

```{r cognitive-duration-by-condition}
cognitive_duration_by_condition <- mixed(
  effort_trial_duration ~ effort_level * condition * effort_task + (1 | id),
  data = cognitive_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(cognitive_duration_by_condition)
```

### Task Comparison

Assignment to task was random, so the tasks can be compared on the post-task
NASA-TLX score, on time on task, and on the error proportion.

```{r cognitive-task-load-comparison}
cognitive_participants <-
  cognitive_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup()

cognitive_participants %>%
  group_by(effort_task) %>%
  summarize(n = n(), mean_tlx = mean(nasa_tlx), sd_tlx = sd(nasa_tlx))

t.test(nasa_tlx ~ effort_task, data = cognitive_participants)
```

Duration partly reflects task mechanics, so it is read alongside the NASA-TLX
comparison.

```{r cognitive-duration-comparison}
cognitive_task_duration <- mixed(
  effort_trial_duration ~ effort_level * effort_task + (1 | id),
  data = cognitive_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)
nice(cognitive_task_duration)

emmeans(cognitive_task_duration, ~ effort_task | effort_level, infer = TRUE)
```

```{r cognitive-error-comparison}
cognitive_task_errors <- mixed(
  effort_error_prop ~ effort_level * effort_task + (1 | id),
  data = cognitive_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)
nice(cognitive_task_errors)

emmeans(cognitive_task_errors, ~effort_task, infer = TRUE)
```

### Beliefs

Post-survey beliefs about how effort relates to liking and to value, pooled
over task and rating condition.

```{r cognitive-beliefs}
belief_summary(bind_rows(cogletters_data, subtractn_data), group = NULL)
```

### Rating Profiles

Each participant did one task in one rating condition, so profiles pool across
the two tasks by condition.

```{r cognitive-profiles}
cognitive_profiles <- derive_effort_profiles(cognitive_data)

summarize_effort_profiles(cognitive_profiles)
```

# Experiment 6A: Buying and Selling Prices, Between Subjects

Participants performed the stepping effort to access artworks and then stated
a price as either buyers or sellers (between subjects), choosing among five
amounts from \$0.10 to \$1.00. The questions are whether effort raises prices
and whether the buyer–seller gap (the endowment pattern) depends on effort.
Every participant who completed the session enters the analyses.

```{r prices-between-data}
prices_between_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/prices_between/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  mutate(
    id = factor(id),
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Buy", "Sell"))
  )

n_prices_between <- n_distinct(prices_between_data$id)
```

The sample comprises `r n_prices_between` participants.

```{r prices-between-sample}
prices_between_data %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarize(n = n_distinct(id))
```

## Main Analysis

One factorial model with role and effort level as fixed effects and a random
intercept per participant carries the effort-by-role question in its
interaction.

```{r prices-between-omnibus}
prices_between_omnibus <- mixed(
  rating ~ condition * effort_level + (1 | id),
  data = prices_between_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(prices_between_omnibus)
```

The effort slope of each role, and their difference, come from the
numeric-effort model.

```{r prices-between-slopes}
prices_between_trend <- mixed(
  rating ~ condition * effort_num + (1 | id),
  data = prices_between_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control, progress = FALSE
)

prices_between_slopes <- emtrends(
  prices_between_trend, ~condition, var = "effort_num", infer = TRUE
)
prices_between_slopes

prices_between_slope_diffs <- pairs(prices_between_slopes, infer = TRUE, reverse = TRUE)
prices_between_slope_diffs
```

::: {.callout-note title="Key result"}
```{r prices-between-key-result}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
report_slopes(prices_between_slopes, prices_between_slope_diffs,
              labels = c(Buy = "Buyer", Sell = "Seller"))
```
:::

The means are plotted with those of Experiment 6B (Both Experiments, below).

## Time on Task

The role-by-effort interaction should hold with performance time in the
model.

```{r prices-between-omnibus-time}
prices_between_omnibus_time <- mixed(
  rating ~ condition * effort_level + effort_time + (1 | id),
  data = prices_between_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(prices_between_omnibus_time)
```

Time on task should track effort level but not the role participants were
assigned to.

```{r prices-between-duration}
prices_between_duration <- mixed(
  effort_time ~ condition * effort_level + (1 | id),
  data = prices_between_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(prices_between_duration)
```

# Experiment 6B: Buying and Selling Prices, Within Subjects

Participants stated both buying and selling prices (within subjects) for
artworks collected at three effort levels, replicating Experiment 6A's
questions with a within-subjects role manipulation. The design, sample size,
and exclusions were preregistered: the analyzed sample excludes participants
who failed an attention check (the in-task check, or the role-order question
answered inconsistently with their actual order), whose summed clicking time
exceeded the sample mean by more than 2.5 SD, or who did not complete the
post-survey, and a skipped rating drops only its trial.

```{r prices-within-data}
prices_within_data <-
  read_csv(here("experiments/prices_within/data/main.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  set_effort_levels() %>%
  mutate(
    id = as.factor(id),
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Buyer", "Seller"))
  )

n_prices_within <- n_distinct(prices_within_data$id)
```

The analyzed sample comprises `r n_prices_within` participants.

```{r prices-within-sample}
prices_within_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  summarize(
    n = n_distinct(id),
    mean_age = mean(age), sd_age = sd(age),
    n_male = n_distinct(id[gender == "Male"]),
    n_female = n_distinct(id[gender == "Female"]),
    n_other = n_distinct(id[gender == "Other"])
  )
```

## Main Analysis

One factorial model with role and effort level as within-subjects fixed effects
and a random intercept per participant carries the effort-by-role question in
its interaction, and the numeric-effort model gives the slope of each role and
their difference.

```{r prices-within-omnibus}
prices_within_omnibus <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_level * condition + (1 | id),
  data = prices_within_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control
)

nice(prices_within_omnibus)
```

```{r prices-within-slopes}
prices_within_trend <- mixed(
  rating ~ effort_num * condition + (1 | id),
  data = prices_within_data,
  method = "S", control = evl_lmer_control, progress = FALSE
)

prices_within_slopes <- emtrends(
  prices_within_trend, ~condition, var = "effort_num", infer = TRUE
)
prices_within_slopes

prices_within_slope_diffs <- pairs(prices_within_slopes, infer = TRUE, reverse = TRUE)
prices_within_slope_diffs
```

::: {.callout-note title="Key result"}
```{r prices-within-key-result}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
report_slopes(prices_within_slopes, prices_within_slope_diffs)
```
:::

## Rating Profiles

Each participant's mean price at high versus low effort classifies them as
increasing or decreasing, separately as buyer and as seller.

```{r prices-within-profiles}
prices_within_profiles <- derive_effort_profiles(prices_within_data)

summarize_effort_profiles(prices_within_profiles)
```

## Both Experiments

Experiments 6A and 6B share one figure, one panel per experiment, each on its
own price scale: Experiment 6A's stated prices (\$0.10–\$1.00) on the left and
Experiment 6B's 1–5 ratings (\$100–\$500) on the right. Each panel keeps the
means and intervals of its own section: raw means for Experiment 6A and model
estimates for Experiment 6B.

```{r prices-combined-plot}
prices_within_means <- as.data.frame(
  emmeans(prices_within_omnibus, ~ effort_level * condition)
)

prices_combined_means <-
  bind_rows(
    prices_between_data %>%
      group_by(condition, effort_level) %>%
      summarize(mean_cl_normal(rating), .groups = "drop") %>%
      transmute(
        experiment = "Experiment 6A", effort_level,
        role = recode(as.character(condition), "Buy" = "Buyer", "Sell" = "Seller"),
        emmean = y, lower.CL = ymin, upper.CL = ymax
      ),
    prices_within_means %>%
      transmute(
        experiment = "Experiment 6B", effort_level, role = as.character(condition),
        emmean, lower.CL, upper.CL
      )
  )

prices_combined_plot <-
  prices_combined_means %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = effort_level, y = emmean, group = role, colour = role)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(aes(fill = role), shape = 21) +
  scale_evl(name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(Buyer = evl_colours[["Open"]], Seller = evl_colours[["Seller"]]), name = NULL
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~experiment, scales = "free_y") +
  ggh4x::facetted_pos_scales(y = list(
    experiment == "Experiment 6A" ~ scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0.10, 1.00), breaks = c(0.10, 0.25, 0.45, 0.75, 1.00),
      labels = scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 0.01), oob = scales::oob_keep
    ),
    experiment == "Experiment 6B" ~ scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(1, 5), breaks = 1:5, labels = label_price, oob = scales::oob_keep
    )
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "Buying and Selling Prices",
    subtitle = "Experiments 6A and 6B",
    x = "Effort Level", y = "Mean Price"
  ) +
  theme_evl(legend = "bottom")

save_figure(prices_combined_plot, "prices_combined_ratings")
```

# Summary

Two quantities carry every experiment's result: the linear effort slope of each
judgment and the difference between the slopes of the two judgments, Δb, taken
as the judgment expected to rise with effort (price, or the selling price) minus
the judgment expected to fall (liking, or the buying price). The table gathers
them with each sample's size, including Experiment S7, the post-effort target
reveal, and the pooled cognitive sample of Experiment 5, which is also listed by
task and, for serial subtraction, at higher task load (+1 SD), where its
dissociation appears. The summary file also carries each slope as a
standardized effect, d, which the overview compares across experiments; the
task-load row is scaled by the rating SD of its task, like the task's own row.

```{r summary}
main_summary <- bind_rows(
  key_result("Experiment 1", "Experiment 1: Laboratory Stepping", n_stepping,
             stepping_slopes, stepping_slope_diffs, "Liking", "Value",
             model = stepping_trend),
  key_result("Experiment 2", "Experiment 2: Observed Effort", n_observed,
             observed_slopes, observed_slope_diffs, "Liking", "Value",
             model = observed_trend),
  key_result("Experiment 3", "Experiment 3: Within-Subjects Clicking", n_clicking_within,
             clicking_within_slopes, clicking_within_slope_diffs, "Liking", "Value",
             model = clicking_within_trend),
  key_result("Experiment 4", "Experiment 4: Effort-Contingent Reveal", n_reveal,
             reveal_slopes, reveal_slope_diffs, "Liking", "Value",
             model = reveal_trend),
  key_result("Experiment S7", "Experiment S7: Post-Effort Target Reveal", n_reveal_endpoint,
             reveal_endpoint_slopes, reveal_endpoint_slope_diffs, "Liking", "Value",
             model = reveal_endpoint_trend),
  key_result("Experiment 5", "Experiment 5: Cognitive Effort", n_cogletters + n_subtractn,
             cognitive_slopes, cognitive_slope_diffs, "Liking", "Value",
             model = cognitive_trend),
  key_result("Experiment 5", "Experiment 5: Letter Transposition", n_cogletters,
             cogletters_slopes, cogletters_slope_diffs, "Liking", "Value",
             model = cogletters_trend, subset = "Letter transposition"),
  key_result("Experiment 5", "Experiment 5: Serial Subtraction", n_subtractn,
             subtractn_slopes, subtractn_slope_diffs, "Liking", "Value",
             model = subtractn_trend, subset = "Serial subtraction"),
  key_result("Experiment 5", "Experiment 5: Serial Subtraction, Moderation by Task Load",
             n_subtractn, subtractn_high_load_slopes, subtractn_high_load_slope_diffs,
             "Liking", "Value", model = subtractn_trend,
             subset = "Serial subtraction, higher task load (+1 SD)"),
  key_result("Experiment 6A", "Experiment 6A: Buying and Selling Prices, Between Subjects",
             n_prices_between, prices_between_slopes, prices_between_slope_diffs, "Buy", "Sell",
             model = prices_between_trend),
  key_result("Experiment 6B", "Experiment 6B: Buying and Selling Prices, Within Subjects",
             n_prices_within, prices_within_slopes, prices_within_slope_diffs, "Buyer", "Seller",
             model = prices_within_trend)
)

main_summary %>%
  transmute(
    study, subset, n,
    falls = sprintf("%s: %.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", falls, falls_b, falls_lower, falls_upper),
    rises = sprintf("%s: %.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", rises, rises_b, rises_lower, rises_upper),
    difference = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f], t(%.0f) = %.2f",
                         delta, delta_lower, delta_upper, delta_df, delta_t)
  )

write_csv(main_summary, here("output/key_results_main.csv"))
```
